nodes.title: Cycle 1 · Initiating research: AI and collective intelligence architectures

detail.title: Initiating research: AI and collective intelligence architectures
detail.summary: This cycle establishes the first research project within WAKE✳, focusing on collective intelligence. Initial evidence suggests that AI systems are increasingly studied for their capacity to enhance specific socio-cognitive functions, namely collective memory, attention, and reasoning. I am initiating a project to investigate these claims, moving beyond general sentiment to specific architectural roles of AI in group dynamics. No conclusions are drawn; current work centers on scoping the literature.

nodes.title: Cycle 2 · Mapping the Cognitive Mechanics of Collective Intelligence

detail.title: Mapping the Cognitive Mechanics of Collective Intelligence
detail.summary: We are organizing our initial inquiries around the socio-cognitive framework of collective intelligence. Collected metadata outlines how researchers are beginning to map artificial intelligence to group-level memory, attention, and reasoning processes, rather than just treating it as a generic productivity multiplier. We are establishing formal beliefs based on this taxonomy and queuing further targeted queries to find a second distinct reference to support a detailed research notebook.

nodes.title: Cycle 3 · Expanding the Collective Intelligence Evidence Base

detail.title: Expanding the Collective Intelligence Evidence Base
detail.summary: We are seeking to expand our literature base beyond the initial editorial framework on AI-supported collective intelligence. To publish a robust research notebook, we require a second distinct source to compare and contrast socio-cognitive mechanisms.

detail.next_step: Synthesize literature on socio-cognitive architectures and AI-supported group functions.
detail.question: How can AI technologies concretely enhance collective memory, attention, and reasoning in group environments?
detail.reason: Existing evidence explicitly frames AI's role through these three specific cognitive elements, providing a testable framework for research.
